findings.title: Deauthentication / disassociation flood
findings.detail: 19 deauth-class frames from 04:42:1a:19:88:f8 inside a 5-second window -- the signature of a forced disconnect, used either as denial of service or to make a client reconnect so its four-way handshake can be captured
evidence: 35 frames total, peak 19 within 5 s starting at t+10.32 s
reason codes seen: 7 (class 3 frame received from nonassociated STA)
none were protected, so every one of them is forgeable by any device in range
findings.benign_explanation: an access point rebooting, shedding clients under load, or steering a client to another band also emits deauths, though rarely this many this fast from one address

findings.title: Possible association disruption: conflicting AP responses
findings.detail: 2 connection attempts by 62:02:b7:f7:a3:c4 to AP 04:42:1a:19:88:f8 received an unprotected disconnect and then a successful association response from the same claimed AP. This inconsistent state can indicate spoofed pre-key disconnects, including on PMF-required networks
evidence: association request frame 1354, unprotected disconnect frame 1355 (reason 6), followed by successful association response within 1 s
association request frame 1925, unprotected disconnect frame 1926 (reason 6), followed by successful association response within 1 s
findings.benign_explanation: capture reordering, stale retransmissions, or an AP firmware/state mismatch may also produce conflicting responses; this is a suspected disruption, not proof

findings.title: Unprotected deauth on an MFP-required network
findings.detail: "testnetworkRPT88" (04:42:1a:19:88:f8) requires management frame protection. Established protected associations should reject forged unprotected disconnects, but frames sent before key installation can still disrupt connection setup; this capture alone does not establish whether the frames were effective
